meta.title: ONE CREDIT JAM #07
meta.reviewed: Reviewed by hand after extract_style.py (draft kept in build/draft/). Kept: every palette role except muted, the two pixel faces and their OFL files, radius 0, dark theme. Changed: purpose, mood, muted, mono/serif stacks, type scale/weights/tracking, margin/grid, HUD, captions, pace, motion, transitions, visual sources, characters, dataViz, post, the whole sound block, narration, paletteAlt (removed). Added: the 16 indexed CREDIT-16 colours and the pixel console spec (top-level 'pixel'). Rationale cites the evidence ids in style-extract.md.

source.notes: jam README: arcade voice (ALL-CAPS headings, caps ratio 0.30), INSERT COIN tagline, five rules (72 HOURS, 16 COLOURS, 320 × 180, 4 CHANNELS, 1 CREDIT), the CREDIT-16 table with roles per colour, dates, WORDS WE USE rules, fictional disclaimer

the palette itself, in index order (also credit16.gpl, credit16.pal and the swatch strip credit16.png); the extractor reads none of the three palette formats, only the PNG strip and the same values as CSS tokens

jam page: 16 indexed colour tokens and role tokens (style.css), Press Start 2P + Silkscreen @font-face, image-rendering: pixelated, a 4-px scanline overlay, a 0.834-s steps() blink, the HUD row 1UP / HI 072016 / CREDIT 00, site.webmanifest
sound rule: PULSE 1, PULSE 2, TRIANGLE, NOISE; 60-Hz tick; house tempo 144 BPM (25 ticks per beat); the attract tune INSERT COIN in D mixolydian; SFX recipes
the jam's own pixel mock-ups (also logo.png and level.png): 320 × 180 art scaled ×4 nearest, CREDIT-16 only; the token hero and the bug come from level.png
Press Start 2P (8-px design grid) and Silkscreen Regular/Bold (5-px caps), SIL OFL 1.1, licences beside the files

rationale.palette: CREDIT-16 is the law of this world (README rule 2: 'No other colours, no alpha blending' [E1]); every role is one of its 16 colours and the reel draws only with the 16 indexed keys (void … peach, in palette order [E28, source/palette/credit16.hex]). Kept from the draft: dark theme (page, manifest and attract screen are VOID [E25, E32, E42, E19]), bg VOID #0B0A16, bg2/surface NIGHT #1E1B3A (the .rule panels [E28]), ink BONE #FFF6E3 [E34], ink2 FOG #A8ADC6 (--text-dim), accent GOLD #FFD93D (--primary, the .btn fill, manifest theme_color, 'coins, credits, the player' [E10, E39, E41]), accent2 CHERRY (1UP), accent3 SKY (links, 2UP), ok LIME, warn EMBER, deny CHERRY, line SLATE, onAccent VOID [E38]. Changed: muted was a derived #7D7876 that is not in the palette; it is FOG (the page's footer and small-print colour, 8.9:1 on VOID). Removed: the derived light paletteAlt (#FBF8F2 …), which is not CREDIT-16 and has no scene to serve (every scene is the same CRT). Dark colours (COBALT, GRAPE, SLATE, RUST, PINE) are fills only; text uses BONE, FOG, GOLD, SKY, LIME, EMBER, BUBBLE or CHERRY (all ≥ 4.7:1 on VOID).
rationale.type: Two pixel faces, as on the jam page [E26, E27, E29–E31, E35]: Press Start 2P (8-px grid, caps 7 px) for titles, HUD and numbers, Silkscreen (5-px caps) for small print, both embedded from source/fonts (OFL [E43–E45]). The draft's stacks fell back to Helvetica/Arial and put JetBrains Mono in mono (the extractor files pixel faces under 'grotesk' and has no pixel category); every role now resolves to the two pixel faces with a monospace fallback, and mono is Press Start 2P (its 8-px cells are monospaced). Sizes are whole multiples of the 8-px cell at the console's ×6 scale (48, 96, 144, 192, 288 px at 1080p) because README rule 3 allows 'whole numbers only' and type is drawn on the 320 × 180 canvas, never scaled smoothly. displayWeight/bodyWeight 400 (Press Start 2P has one weight; the draft's synthetic 800 would smear the pixels); tracking 0 (the cell carries its own 1-px gap).
rationale.motion: Energetic: an attract loop that shouts (ALL-CAPS ratio 0.30, one rule per line [E1]) at the house tempo of 144 BPM [E23]; the draft's 'medium' came from '!' and emoji counts, which this README barely uses, and it does not read caps. Motion is the console's, not a motion designer's curves: sprites live on the 320 × 180 grid and move in whole pixels, stepped at 12 fps on the 60-fps timeline (a beat is exactly 5 steps at 144 BPM), with constant run speeds, gravity arcs and hard landings (ease lin); springs only pop score text. Screen shake moves the game world by whole pixels while the HUD row stays put. Transitions: hard cuts, the game's own palette flashes and fades, mosaic and iris wipes drawn on the canvas, and the compositor's cut, flash, strobe and glitch (a CRT signal hit); the draft's zoomInto and whip are smooth camera moves that would smear the pixel grid and slide the CRT glass. Reveals: typing (letter by letter) and slot-reel digit spins. characters: true (changed): the GOLD token with sneakers is 'the player' in the jam's own mock-up [E10, E21]; it is drawn in code as pixel sprites. dataViz: false (changed): data 0.66 came from the palette table, hex codes and dates, not from measurements.
rationale.sound: The material states its sound: four chip channels (two pulse, triangle, noise), a 60-Hz tick, the house tempo 144 BPM and the attract tune INSERT COIN in D mixolydian [E23]. The draft (dark-synth, 125 BPM, A minor) followed the dark theme and could not reach 144 inside dark-synth's 118–130 range. Key D (also what the extractor's hue mapping gives GOLD); sound.mode is major until the validator accepts the schema's church modes, the tune itself is mixolydian (sound.chip.mode). BPM 144 also makes 15 s = 9 bars and 30 s = 18 bars exactly and a bar = 100 frames at 60 fps. No preset in audio/synth.py plays chip channels yet: preset bright-pop and its plucks/lead/bass/kit stand in for the timing draft, and sound.chip records the target voices and the jam's SFX recipes for the audio pass. SFX family digital (bleeps) until a chip family exists.
rationale.narration: Not recommended (changed): an arcade attract loop and a jam launch teaser, music-led; the draft's purpose 'docs' came from tables and section counts, not from the voice of the material. Every idea is on screen as type, so muted autoplay works. If a voice is ever wanted it is an announcer, not an explainer: Puck, [bright, playful], en-GB (the README spells 'colours' and asks for it [E1]).
rationale.visuals: Carrier: code-drawn pixel art only (vector): a 320 × 180 indexed canvas per scene, scaled ×6 nearest and shown through a code-drawn CRT (scanlines, slight curvature, phosphor glow via post.bloom) because the jam page itself overlays scanlines and renders pixelated [source/site/style.css]. The draft's app-ui and web-shots are dropped: the material's screens are mock-ups (README disclaimer), and a browser capture of the jam page would be a smooth web page, not the console. The token hero, the bug, the gems and the logo lockup follow the jam's own mock-ups [E18, E19, E21].

fonts.cjk: "Pretendard", "Apple SD Gothic Neo", "Noto Sans CJK KR", "Noto Sans CJK JP", sans-serif

pixel.rationale: README rule 3 (320 × 180, whole-number scaling, square pixels, no smoothing) and the jam page (--px, image-rendering: pixelated, a scanline overlay) [E1, source/site/style.css]; ×6 fills 1920 × 1080 exactly. stepFps 12 on the 60-fps timeline: at 144 BPM a beat is 25 frames = 5 steps, so every stepped pose lands on the beat grid. palette lists the CREDIT-16 keys in index order (00 VOID … 15 PEACH).

chip.status: chip voices live in audio/synth.py (chip_pulse, chip_tri, chip_noise); preset chiptune

channels.name: PULSE 1
channels.job: lead melody, coin and jump blips

channels.name: NOISE
channels.job: snare, hats, explosions, the coin slot

chip.mix: mono, no reverb, no filters, 16 volume steps
chip.tune: INSERT COIN, D mixolydian, 4-bar loop: PULSE 1 hook, PULSE 2 arpeggios on D, C, G, TRIANGLE walking bass, NOISE kick-snare on 1 and 3 with closed hats on every 8th

sfx.coin: PULSE 1, duty 50 %, B5 then E6, 4 ticks each
sfx.jump: PULSE 1, duty 25 %, slide up an octave over 10 ticks
sfx.stomp: NOISE short mode, 6 ticks + TRIANGLE drop
sfx.hit: NOISE long mode + PULSE 1 sliding down two octaves
sfx.highscore: PULSE 1 + PULSE 2 in octaves, eight fast notes up the scale
